title: CBS Radio Mystery Theater
paragraphs: Himan Brown's hour-long dramatic anthology revived radio mystery for a later generation with stories of crime, horror, the supernatural, science fiction, and suspense, most famously hosted by E. G.
Himan Brown’s CBS dramatic anthology revived network radio drama in 1974. The archive distinguishes 1,399 numbered original programs from later repeat broadcasts.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: E. G. Marshall host era (January 6, 1974 to January 29, 1982) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Tammy Grimes final host era (February 1, 1982 to December 7, 1982) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include E. G. Marshall (host and performer), Himan Brown (director, producer, and host), Ian Martin (performer, writer, and radio adaptor), Sam Dann (writer, radio adaptor, and author), Robert Dryden (performer), Bryna Raeburn (performer), and Marian Seldes (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].
The stories often return to Murder, Supernatural phenomena, War and military conflict, Medicine and psychology, Occult and curses, and Trials and legal process.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Network radio drama revival in the television era, Sponsor-supported national radio drama in the 1970s, and Golden-age radio veterans alongside newer stage and screen actors.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], and [[show|the-chase|The Chase]].
